subject: chemistry
title: Word, balanced and ionic equations
key_idea: An equation shows the reactants and products of a reaction. A balanced symbol equation has the same number of each type of atom on both sides. An ionic equation shows only the ions that react.

blocks.text: A chemical reaction can be written as a word equation or as a symbol equation. Both have reactants on the left and products on the right.

items.meaning: A substance that is used up in a reaction.
A substance that is made in a reaction.
An equation that gives the names of the reactants and products.

blocks.label: A word equation
where: The reactants are on the left of the arrow.
The product is on the right of the arrow.

items: Write the full name of every substance.
Take care with names. Ammonia and ammonium are different substances.
Use the arrow to show that the reactants form the products.
H₂O(g) is water vapour, also called steam.
A molten substance is a liquid, so it is shown as (l).
A solution in water is (aq), not (l).
A word equation uses names. Reactants are on the left and products on the right.
The four state symbols are (s), (l), (g) and (aq).

blocks.text: Atoms are not made or destroyed in a reaction. A balanced equation has the same number of each type of atom on both sides.

blocks.label: A balanced symbol equation with state symbols
where: The big number in front of a formula multiplies the whole formula.
The small number below an element (subscript) is part of the formula.
Two Mg and two O on each side.

items.text: Write the correct formula of each reactant and product.
Count each type of atom on both sides.
Put numbers in front of formulae until each atom type matches.
Count every atom type on both sides.

items: Never change a subscript to balance an equation. Changing it makes a different substance.
Balancing marks depend on the formulae being correct.
Any correct multiple of the equation is allowed, such as halves or doubles.

diagram.alt: Put the steps for balancing a symbol equation in order.
diagram.prompt: Put the steps for balancing an equation in order.
steps: Write the correct formula of each reactant and product
Count each type of atom on both sides
Put a number in front of a formula to balance one atom type
Count each type of atom on both sides again

items: Balance by changing the big numbers in front of formulae, never the small ones.
Atoms are conserved, so each type has the same count on both sides.
Include state symbols when asked.

blocks.text: (Higher tier) An ionic equation shows only the ions or particles that change. It leaves out the ions that are the same on both sides.

items.meaning: An equation showing only the ions and substances that take part in the reaction.
An ion that is in the mixture but does not change in the reaction.

blocks.label: Ionic equation for a precipitate
where: Mg²⁺(aq) is the magnesium ion in solution.
OH⁻(aq) is the hydroxide ion in solution.

items.text: Write the balanced equation with state symbols.
Write each (aq) ionic compound as separate ions.
Cross out any ion that is the same on both sides.
The atoms and the charges must balance.

items: Solids, liquids and gases are not split into ions.
Charges must balance. In the example, 2+ and 2 × 1− gives zero, the charge on Mg(OH)₂.
A displacement reaction can also be an ionic equation: Mg(s) + Zn²⁺(aq) → Mg²⁺(aq) + Zn(s).

diagram.alt: Put the steps for writing an ionic equation in order.
diagram.prompt: Put the steps for writing an ionic equation in order.
steps: Write the balanced equation with state symbols
Write each aqueous ionic compound as separate ions
Cross out the ions that are the same on both sides
Write the equation with the ions that are left
Check that the atoms and charges balance

items: An ionic equation shows only the particles that change.
Spectator ions are the same on both sides and are left out.
Atoms and charges must both balance.

checks.q: Write the word equation for ammonia reacting with nitric acid to make ammonium nitrate.
Balance the equation: K + Br₂ → KBr. Add state symbols for solid potassium, bromine gas and solid potassium bromide.
(Higher tier) Write the ionic equation for iron(II) ions reacting with hydroxide ions to form the precipitate iron(II) hydroxide, Fe(OH)₂.

mistakes.right: The state symbol (g) means gas. Write water vapour, steam or gaseous water.

mistakes.wrong: Mg + Zn²⁺ → Mg²⁺ + Zn, with no state symbols.
mistakes.right: The question asks for state symbols. Write Mg(s) + Zn²⁺(aq) → Mg²⁺(aq) + Zn(s). A mark is lost if the symbols are missing or incorrect.

mistakes.wrong: Ammonium nitrate solution has the state symbol (l).
mistakes.right: A solution in water is aqueous. The state symbol is (aq).

worked_example.question:
Magnesium displaces zinc from zinc sulfate solution.

Complete the ionic equation for the reaction.

You should include state symbols.

Mg(s) + Zn²⁺(aq) → _________ + _________
answer_points: Mg²⁺(aq) is the magnesium ion in solution.
Zn(s) is the zinc metal formed as a solid.
worked_example.tip: Multiples are allowed. One mark is available for the correct species even if state symbols are missing or incorrect.

exam_phrases: balancing of correct species / formulae only
allow multiples; ignore incorrect state symbols (ionic equations)

mistakes.wrong: ammonia sulfate or ammonium for ammonia in a word equation.
mistakes.right: These names are rejected. Write ammonia + sulfuric acid → ammonium sulfate.

mistakes.wrong: 2NH₃ + H₂SO₄ → NH₄SO₄, balanced with the wrong formula for ammonium sulfate.
mistakes.right: The balancing mark depends on the formula of the product being correct. Ammonium sulfate is (NH₄)₂SO₄, so 2NH₃ + H₂SO₄ → (NH₄)₂SO₄.
This is not balanced. Two hydroxide ions are needed: Fe²⁺ + 2OH⁻ → Fe(OH)₂. Marks are given for each side and for balancing the correct species.

worked_example.question:
Iron(II) sulfate solution reacts with sodium hydroxide solution to form a pale green precipitate of iron(II) hydroxide, Fe(OH)₂.

Write the ionic equation for this reaction.
answer_points: Balancing of the correct species: Fe²⁺ + 2OH⁻ → Fe(OH)₂ (1)
worked_example.tip: Allow multiples. Incorrect state symbols are ignored.

exam_phrases: allow any correct multiple, including fractions

mistakes.wrong: Mg²⁺ and OH⁻ → Mg(OH)₂, using 'and' between the ions.
mistakes.right: 'And' and '&' are not allowed instead of '+'. Write Mg²⁺ + 2OH⁻ → Mg(OH)₂.

mistakes.wrong: NaO + H₂O → 2NaOH, balanced by changing the formula of sodium oxide.
mistakes.right: The formulae must be correct, because the balancing mark depends on them. Sodium oxide is Na₂O.

mistakes.wrong: Ba²⁺ + SO₄²⁻ → BaSO₄, with no state symbols when state symbols are asked for.
mistakes.right: Include the symbols: Ba²⁺ (aq) + SO₄²⁻ (aq) → BaSO₄ (s). The state symbol mark depends on the correct species.

worked_example.question:
Magnesium nitrate is an ionic compound.

A solution containing magnesium ions reacts with a solution containing hydroxide ions.

Solid magnesium hydroxide is made.

Write the balanced ionic equation for this reaction.
answer_points: Correct formulae: Mg²⁺, OH⁻ and Mg(OH)₂ (1)
worked_example.tip: State symbols are ignored in this question. Any correct multiple is allowed.
